01_DSN_2027.paper: Recoverable Safety Journals for Crash-Consistent AI-Mediated Health-State Mutations
01_DSN_2027.novelty: Recoverability is a safety property of the *joint* clinical row, immutable decision lineage, and asynchronous side-effect record, not just of one database commit. Define a recoverable outcome function that returns COMMITTED, REJECTED, or INDETERMINATE until reconcilable ground truth exists.
01_DSN_2027.gap: Transactional outbox and database WAL already give crash-safe writes; the unresolved issue worth testing is whether an AI proposal lineage and user-visible decision stay consistent across crash windows and arbitrary duplicate deliveries. Without a new counterexample to a careful outbox baseline, this is an application paper, not a DSN A contribution.
rqs: RQ1: Across crash cut points, are there executions where the clinical state, decision receipt, and outbox state disagree after bounded recovery?
RQ2: Under at-least-once replay and concurrent consent revocation, does recovery preserve idempotence, causal order, and correct INDETERMINATE labels?
RQ3: What is the added durable-write, p99 latency and recovery-time cost compared with transactional outbox and durable workflow baselines?
01_DSN_2027.falsify: If a correctly engineered PostgreSQL transaction + outbox + idempotent consumer achieves the same invariants and equal/better recovery cost, discard the new mechanism superiority claim.
baseline: DB transaction only + fire-and-forget side effect
weak control; measures lost side effects
PostgreSQL atomic write + transactional outbox + idempotent consumer
strong practical baseline; must implement fully
Durable workflow/saga with compensation and stable operation IDs
strong operational baseline; record precise engine/version
metrics: orphan clinical writes per independent history
01_DSN_2027.design: A reconciler checks a versioned decision receipt against the committed row, independent outbox receipt and consent epoch. Invalid/ambiguous evidence never becomes a positive outcome; retry decisions are keyed to immutable operation IDs.
01_DSN_2027.dataset: Generate 48 crash windows x 4 commit/revocation orderings x 3 delivery schedules x 5 independent seeds. Confirm final N only after schedule deduplication; benchmark 1/2/4/8 worker settings.
01_DSN_2027.oracle: Jepsen/Elle-compatible history export plus deterministic SQL-state audit; manually review anomaly witnesses.
01_DSN_2027.risks: Very high novelty bar, deadline nearly immediate. Do not submit a routine outbox implementation as a breakthrough.

02_PoPETs_2027.paper: Revocation-Complete Future Disclosure for Cached Longitudinal AI Contexts
02_PoPETs_2027.novelty: Define *future dispatch noninterference* under consent revocation for every derivation path (prompt segment, cached summary, embedding pointer, retry payload, and fallback transport). Provide a dependency-closure invalidation algorithm and leakage audit that explicitly excludes information already delivered to any external provider.
02_PoPETs_2027.gap: Existing access control and cache invalidation can block future reads, and machine unlearning targets a different threat. A research gap exists only if persistent indirect derived context, retry queues, and fallback paths cause measurable post-revocation leakage that strong per-use reauthorization baselines miss.
rqs: RQ1: Can any post-revocation model dispatch contain disallowed attributes through transitive caches or retries, even when direct record access is denied?
RQ2: Does origin- and purpose-labeled dependency closure match a full always-recompute authorized view on disclosure traces?
RQ3: What are cache hit, bytes transferred, re-computation, false invalidation and authorized utility costs at increasing lineage density?
02_PoPETs_2027.falsify: If complete per-dispatch authorization + recompute matches the candidate with negligible overhead and zero leakage, narrow novelty to an engineering performance trade-off; never assert erasure of prior external disclosures.
baseline: coarse cache purge on consent change
privacy reference upper bound, cost comparator
strong architecture baseline if adapter truly supports derivations
02_PoPETs_2027.design: For grant g, purpose p, and dispatch d after revocation time t_r, require forbidden_label(g,p) ∩ lineage(d)=∅ under a declared observation model. Label derived artifacts at creation; invalidate reverse edges on revocation; reauthorize at every dispatch.
02_PoPETs_2027.dataset: Synthetic 1200 unique subjects with 3-6 longitudinal contexts each; factorial lineage fanout, delayed cache writes, retries, and policy changes; source-disjoint holdout; label N by subject not number of dispatches.
02_PoPETs_2027.oracle: Independent recomputation of all live-purpose permission clauses from source snapshots; byte-level dispatch interceptor and sealed cancellation log.
02_PoPETs_2027.risks: Inability to retract already delivered content must be stated prominently. Post-revocation future leakage only; no claim of cryptographic retroactive erasure.

03_IFIP_SEC_2027.paper: Replay-Closed Authorization Across Purpose, Delegation, and AI Proposal Lineage
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.novelty: Study a *multi-principal interleaving* in which a valid consent-purpose receipt is delegated, refreshed and consumed across policy-epoch changes and concurrent replay. Define a consumed-once invariant and a tested provenance binding for delegated proposal chains.
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.gap: Macaroons and Zanzibar already solve substantial parts of contextual authorization and consistency. A credible new claim must show a specific multi-hop lineage/replay counterexample against strong correctly configured caveat-token and versioned authorization baselines, not just signature checking.
rqs: RQ1: Under which delegation and epoch interleavings do signed context-bound capability baselines admit an invalid replay or reject valid operations?
RQ2: Is the proposed consume-once transition linearizable under two or more real PostgreSQL sessions and revoked scope?
RQ3: What are token size, verification latency and legitimate operation rejection costs relative to well-configured Macaroons and Zanzibar-like policies?
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.falsify: If a properly scoped Macaroon plus consistent authorization check is decision-equivalent on all attacks, state equivalence and do not claim stronger security.
baseline: Macaroon HMAC caveats: actor, purpose, task, expiry, nonce
Zanzibar/OpenFGA with consistency token and fresh policy evaluation
Cedar/OPA policy decision with replay nonce registry
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.design: Receipts are typed commitments: HMAC over actor, patient, tenant, purpose, task, consent/policy epoch, dispatch digest, nonce and parent reference. Verify the full delegation ancestry and atomically consume the nonce, not just signature equality.
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.dataset: Distinct 900 adversarial interleavings in isolated synthetic accounts across delegation/revocation/retry/tenant switches; clean controls matched per threat family.
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.oracle: Independent allow/deny oracle based on frozen principal graph and commit-time consent epoch, not candidate verifier output.
03_IFIP_SEC_2027.risks: Potentially weak novelty relative to existing capability systems; reject manuscript if B1/B2 already meet every invariant.

04_ACNS_2027.paper: SoK: Evidence Boundaries of Attestation in Tool-Using AI Systems
04_ACNS_2027.novelty: An evidence-to-claim lattice for assembly, egress, transport acknowledgment, provider-attested receipt, execution trace and semantic consumption, with mechanized *counterexample witnesses* showing which implications fail absent explicit trust assumptions.
04_ACNS_2027.gap: Existing cryptographic attestation terminology (IETF RATS) and agent safety benchmarks address related but nonidentical assurance claims. A SoK contributes only if its systematic taxonomy is reproducible, independently double-coded and resolves real disagreements, not if it rebrands provenance as new.
rqs: RQ1: Which attestation claims are actually supported by which observable evidence and trusted parties in published agent systems?
RQ2: Which claimed implication pairs are invalid under explicit adversarial and provider models, and can small executable witnesses demonstrate this?
RQ3: How consistently can independent reviewers classify claims and reproduce counterexamples across a pre-registered corpus?
04_ACNS_2027.falsify: If taxonomy fails coder agreement or merely restates RFC 9334 / existing provenance literature without new cases and insights, do not claim SoK contribution.
baseline: W3C PROV provenance and audit events
AgentDojo/ToolEmu evidence and attack observability categories
04_ACNS_2027.design: Define observation/trust axes, mechanically enumerate implication candidates, construct counterexamples for false implications, and publish extraction rules and independently adjudicated study selection ledger.
04_ACNS_2027.dataset: Search ACM/IEEE/USENIX/NDSS/ICLR/NeurIPS publications from pre-registered 2019-2026 window; freeze duplicate resolution, screening decisions and extraction workbook.
04_ACNS_2027.oracle: Independent dual human coders; no internal LLM agents represented as independent reviewers.
04_ACNS_2027.risks: ACNS 2027 CFP may not offer SoK-specific track; only submit after checking venue scope and completed original systematic method.

05_COMPSAC_2027.paper: Dependency-Complete Optimistic Admission for Concurrent Clinical AI Writes
05_COMPSAC_2027.novelty: A machine-checkable *dependency-closure oracle* for schema-defined clinical write operations, coupled with scope-local optimistic versioning that minimizes false-stale rejection without allowing write skew under changing consent and policy.
05_COMPSAC_2027.gap: Silo/OCC and PostgreSQL Serializable Snapshot Isolation already address concurrency; original value must come from automatically deriving semantically required cross-resource dependencies for *AI-generated* clinical writes and quantifying the safety/throughput frontier.
rqs: RQ1: Compared with globally versioned OCC, does a dependency-complete read set reduce unnecessary aborts without increasing forbidden commits?
RQ2: How does omitted dependency failure propagate under explicit write-skew and policy-epoch races, and can a separate oracle detect each flaw?
RQ3: At what graph fanout and contention does dependency-scope overhead erase throughput gains relative to PostgreSQL SERIALIZABLE?
05_COMPSAC_2027.falsify: Any forbidden commit under a complete, independently labeled dependency schedule falsifies the safety claim; if fully serializable PostgreSQL is as fast, candidly report the null performance benefit.
baseline: Silo-style entity readset OCC with commit-time validation
strong algorithmic comparator; disclose that port is not Silo source code
05_COMPSAC_2027.design: Freeze per-operation dependency schema and required read/write edges. Validate all required edge versions and consent/policy epochs in one DB transaction with canonical lock ordering. Export histories to Elle/independent serializability checker.
05_COMPSAC_2027.dataset: Deterministic family of medication/allergy/history/purpose grants; 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 workers; workload partitions with Zipf skew and dependency density; ≥ 5 independent seeds per setting before deciding power.
05_COMPSAC_2027.oracle: Independent dependency oracle plus transaction-history consistency checker; record kernel SHA, PG release/version and isolation setting.
05_COMPSAC_2027.risks: A large/sound baseline (PG SSI) is essential; avoid weak baselines only and never reuse R4 SQLite as PG performance.

06_AIME_2027.paper: Counterfactual Clinical Workflow Safety under Changing Consent and Medication Histories
06_AIME_2027.novelty: A paired *two-axis error decomposition* separating unauthorized data use from clinically incorrect permitted recommendations under longitudinal context change, with avoidable-refusal cost reported rather than hidden.
06_AIME_2027.gap: MedHELM, HealthBench and clinical safety benchmarks evaluate medical quality; existing governance systems evaluate authorization. A joint longitudinal workflow protocol with independent clinician adjudication may expose the gap between clinically correct advice and *permitted* actions.
rqs: RQ1: How often does each method make an action-eligibility mistake versus a clinical-fact omission when medications or consent change during the task?
RQ2: Does purpose-aware selective regeneration preserve appropriate task completion while reducing forbidden data use relative to full restart and static context?
RQ3: Are effects stable across update types, at least two actual providers, and an independent physician-adjudicated case set?
06_AIME_2027.falsify: No clinician reviewer or independent original vignettes = no clinical validity claim. If selective regeneration gains no utility over complete refresh, narrow to a descriptive workflow evaluation.
baseline: full per-step refresh + current policy filter
HealthBench-/MedHELM-informed evaluation rubric for clinical utility
benchmark rubric, not a decision algorithm
06_AIME_2027.design: Compare four truly matched provider-prompt arms on case histories with independently frozen clinical and policy labels. Reviewers separately rate medical appropriateness and authority of used evidence, blinded to method.
06_AIME_2027.dataset: Synthetic source-disjoint vignettes with counterfactual pairs: baseline H, medication update, allergy, revocation, unrelated edit, clinical task. Target N determined by pilot variance and planned power; never label small LLM probes clinical trials.
06_AIME_2027.oracle: Independent authorized evidence oracle and qualified clinician review; patient-level paired bootstrap/clustered CI.
06_AIME_2027.risks: High dependency on physician reviewers, model access costs, and exact clinical statements. Short paper only if results and validation adequate.

07_SACMAT_2027.paper: PolicyTrace: Temporal Conformance Testing of Delegated Consent across Heterogeneous Policy Engines
07_SACMAT_2027.novelty: A *history-sensitive conformance property* for delegated consent and purpose-bound access with trace-level metamorphic test generation and independent oracle adjudication across Cedar, OpenFGA and OPA encodings.
07_SACMAT_2027.gap: MC/DC XACML policy testing and XACBench cover static policy structures; what must be demonstrated as new is systematic conformance testing of policy *histories* with revocation/redelegation and replay, including portability failures attributable to mismatched semantics.
rqs: RQ1: Which distinct trace-level policy errors are undetected by static rule/decision coverage but exposed by temporal metamorphic tests?
RQ2: How many executable mutants representing revocation, delegation, purpose and temporal precedence are killed by comparable budgets for random, MC/DC-inspired and PolicyTrace generation?
RQ3: Across Cedar, OpenFGA and OPA, which semantics are faithfully expressible, and where do adapters necessarily diverge?
07_SACMAT_2027.falsify: If trace generator does not outperform stateful and MC/DC-guided baselines at equal oracle-call budget, do not claim novel fault detection; publish portability limits transparently.
baseline: MC/DC-inspired XACML policy testing (Xu et al. SACMAT 2018)
property-based history generator without temporal metamorphs
metrics: mutation score at fixed oracle budget
07_SACMAT_2027.design: Define a portable three/four-valued decision oracle (PERMIT/DENY/NOT_APPLICABLE/INDETERMINATE) and a partial mapping to each PDP; test revocation-before-replay, delegation expiration, explicit-deny precedence and temporal reorderings.
07_SACMAT_2027.dataset: Versioned synthetic policy and principal graphs + 50 independently designed mutants; reserve fresh holdout mutant families; source/seed freeze prior to scoring.
07_SACMAT_2027.oracle: Executable declarative reference semantics and independent human review of semantically non-equivalent mutants.
07_SACMAT_2027.risks: SACMAT Dataset/Tool track is likely better than a main claim. Need actual external engine execution rather than merely naming them.

08_DIMVA_2027.paper: GovernanceTrace: Detecting Adaptive Authorization-Boundary Probing from Minimal Agent Events
08_DIMVA_2027.novelty: A *privacy-constrained sequence detector* distinguishing benign retry bursts from deliberate multi-step policy/receipt boundary reconnaissance; generalization measured on unseen attack families and tooling changes.
08_DIMVA_2027.gap: AgentDojo and ToolEmu provide realistic agent safety attacks; IDS literature warns models can memorize environments. Novelty demands detector evaluation on independently generated multi-stage traces with constrained PHI metadata and rigorous cross-family holdout, rather than training on rejection reason codes that trivially reveal labels.
rqs: RQ1: Can a detector identify attack campaigns from PHI-minimized events at bounded benign false alarms, without using attack-specific reason-code leakage?
RQ2: How does cross-family/cross-tenant holdout change precision-recall and time-to-detect relative to rule-based, IsolationForest, boosted-tree and sequence models?
RQ3: How do adaptive attacker retries and privacy budgets affect detection and diagnostic reconstruction?
08_DIMVA_2027.falsify: If rule thresholds perform as well as sequence models on family-held-out traces, do not claim ML necessity; if detector depends on post-hoc failure labels, invalidate primary experiment.
baseline: static threshold on failures per window
08_DIMVA_2027.design: Derive minimal log schema independent of raw patient data; split by attack family and synthetic tenant; keep rejection codes masked in leak-safe primary test, then disclose effect of allowing them in an ablation.
08_DIMVA_2027.dataset: Multi-stage synthetic sessions plus benign retries, outages, latency spikes; attacker cannot read privileged logs; frozen family-holdout groups with no shared templates across train/test.
08_DIMVA_2027.oracle: Campaign intent and authorized action adjudicated from simulator ground truth, never from detector score or gateway final reason code.
08_DIMVA_2027.risks: Security venue will require demonstrated attack novelty and realism. Explicit avoid simplistic generated labels.

09_PST_2027.paper: ReceiptMin: Measuring Forensic Reconstructability under Purpose-Bound Audit Minimization
09_PST_2027.novelty: A formally defined *reconstruction-versus-linkability frontier* for AI health action receipts, separating proof of an event commitment from recovery of sensitive content under post-retention access privileges.
09_PST_2027.gap: Hash chains, transparency logs, HMAC identifiers and encryption already exist; a useful contribution requires new quantitative evidence about audit decision reconstructability versus attacker attribute/linkage inference for longitudinal health workflows.
rqs: RQ1: What fraction of legitimate forensic questions remain answerable under hash-only, encrypted, and selective retention receipts?
RQ2: Can linkage and attribute exposure be bounded under compromised read-only audit access, including auxiliary-data joins?
RQ3: What retention, key deletion and proof-generation costs emerge across audit volumes and retention epochs?
09_PST_2027.falsify: If encrypted full logs with a well-managed retention policy dominate minimized receipts on privacy and reconstruction, reject novelty superiority claim.
baseline: utility upper bound / privacy lower bound
encrypted log with role-gated decryption and deletion
RFC 9162-like Merkle append-only integrity + authorized material retrieval
proposed purpose-bound minimized receipt and retention map
09_PST_2027.design: Define forensic query set ex ante; preserve commitment and consent/policy epoch proofs while removing patient detail; test attacker with auxiliary linkage metadata and a realistic audit-reader privilege.
09_PST_2027.dataset: Synthetic records/events with explicit correlation surfaces, varying log sizes, user identifiers, retention windows, backups; externality of key deletion declared in threat model.
09_PST_2027.oracle: Trusted offline complete ledger retained only for evaluation; blinded authorized forensic queries and attacker inference tests.
09_PST_2027.risks: Avoid claiming content deletion from immutable historical disclosures or from unverified cloud backups.
